mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where real GDP declines over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where housing starts decrease by more than 10% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the CPI increases by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) declines and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals a weakening economy with a strained labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer and business confidence wane.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where real GDP declines and the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.3% in a month.
